title: Build Your Own Read-Only Local Agent Audit

sections.title: Spec Your Local Stack
sections.prompt: Write down your own equivalent of the Ollama + Qwen2.5-14B + LangGraph + DuckDB stack: pick a local model your machine can run (check quant size against your RAM), and list the exact tool-calls it gets access to first — file listing, SELECT queries, CSV grep — nothing else, matching the read-only-first rule from the post.

sections.title: Find Your Own Null-Signup Bug
sections.prompt: Take a real table you own with nullable date or category columns and ask: if I dropped every null row right now, what silent business meaning would I destroy? Write the one-line reclassification (like the signup_channel isna().map() fix) that turns the null into signal instead of deleting it.

sections.title: Draw Your Reliable vs Can't-Touch Line
sections.prompt: List 5 tasks you'd hand to a local agent. For each, mark 'Reliable' only if you can verify the answer in under 10 seconds (re-run the query, eyeball the number) and 'Can't touch' if it requires knowing why a number moved or which metric matters for a decision — be honest about which column most tasks land in.

sections.title: Cost the Cloud-vs-Local Tradeoff
sections.prompt: Calculate your own version of the '$60-70/month in API calls' number: estimate how many cleanup/profiling calls you'd make locally in a week, multiply by your current API per-call cost, and compare against the hardware you already own to decide if going local is a real unlock or just a vibe.

sections.title: Write the Escalation Sentence
sections.prompt: Pick a metric your agent (or you) tracks weekly. Write the one sentence a junior analyst should say when the number moves — the 'that's not the question you should be asking' pushback — for a scenario where an external event (pricing change, upstream schema change) makes the raw delta misleading.

cta: Run the null-signup check on one of your own tables and reply with what you found — even if it's 'nothing broke,' that's data too.
